findings.title: Spec text drifted from implemented decisions
findings.problem: Spec section 3 still says IDP-claims D is derived by email and must not key on username, and section 4 still promises LiteLLMContext.budget_target_project; the code treats the username workspace as personal/D and carries the target in budget_fallback_from.
findings.impact: Reviewers and future work read a design that the code deliberately does not follow.
findings.recommendation: Update spec sections 3 and 4 to the implemented behaviour and record them as decisions.

findings.title: Scoped context shares the mutable parent object
findings.problem: scoped_llm_context re-sets the same LiteLLMContext object; _record_direct_budget_attribution mutates it in place, so a nested build that does not call set_llm_context changes the parent's attribution and reset() does not undo it.
findings.impact: Nested model builds can leak a fallback into the parent's analytics and runtime decision.
findings.recommendation: Enter the scope with litellm_context.set(ctx.model_copy() if ctx else None).

findings.title: Reindex of index without project now raises
findings.problem: set_llm_context(self.index, None, user) goes through _asset_project, which raises ExtendedHTTPException when project_name is empty; the line above already guards that case and the old call passed None.
findings.impact: File reindex fails for indexes with an empty project_name where it used to run.
findings.recommendation: Pass the index only when project_name is set, otherwise keep the asset-less call.

findings.title: Personal-context guard compares against username only
findings.problem: has_real_project_context excludes current_project == user_email, but user_email is now the username while a personal charge sets current_project to the email.
findings.impact: A personal charge can be treated as a real project context and re-break the premium budget guard.
findings.recommendation: Also exclude runtime_context.personal_project from the real-project check.

findings.title: Ignored CLI header project still resolves credentials
findings.problem: resolve_litellm_user_credentials runs with the raw header project before attribution, so a non-member project's premium project key can be returned and sent as Authorization; on the personal-key bypass the raw header project also stays in request_info[PROJECT] and reaches analytics.
findings.impact: A project the user is not a member of can be charged and shown in analytics, violating D3 and the security anti-goal.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize request_info[PROJECT] in _extract_request_info to member projects (else the default project or username) so credential lookup, bypass analytics and attribution all use it; keep the raw header only for the ignore log.

findings.title: Global workflow forces saved assistants global
findings.problem: build_agent_for_workflow marks a saved non-global assistant is_global inside a global workflow, so set_llm_context charges D instead of applying rows 1-8 to that assistant.
findings.impact: Row 11 / D2 not met: a member's funded asset project is skipped for saved assistants in marketplace workflows.
findings.recommendation: Attribute billing with the saved assistant's own is_global; keep the override only for inline assistants and non-billing behaviour.

findings.title: Caller project hint used as default without membership
findings.problem: fallback_default (request.project or user.current_project from asset-less routers) becomes D for users without a default and is probed and charged with no membership check.
findings.impact: A request-supplied project the user does not belong to can be probed, flagged and charged.
findings.recommendation: Accept fallback_default only when it is one of the user's member projects or their personal project.

findings.title: Case-insensitive membership crosses distinct projects
findings.problem: _is_member uses casefold, so an asset from project 'Team-A' counts as a member target for a member of 'team-a'; the CLI header is charged in the typed spelling while the funded SQL and LiteLLM are exact.
findings.impact: Membership can be granted across case-variant projects, and a case-variant CLI header misses its funded budget.
findings.recommendation: Use exact membership for assets; for the CLI header map a case variant to the member's own spelling.

findings.title: Cache read can race TTL expiry
findings.problem: _cached_project_budget_scopes checks 'in' for every key and then reads with [], so an entry expiring or evicted in between raises KeyError.
findings.impact: Sporadic KeyError turns a funded project into a fallback or fails CLI budget availability.
findings.recommendation: Read with .get(key, sentinel) once and treat a missing sentinel as a cache miss.

findings.title: resolve_sync keeps a third funded SQL copy
findings.problem: BudgetResolutionService.resolve_sync still has its own inline copy of the funded query.
findings.impact: The spec's single funded definition can drift between paths.
findings.recommendation: Reuse PROJECT_BUDGET_FUNDED_SQL with a single category.

findings.title: Unknown model counts any scope as funded
findings.problem: _unfunded_project returns 'can pay' when the project has any budget category and no model is known (workflows, assistants without llm_model_type); at model build the real category is unfunded and llm_factory falls straight to personal without trying D.
findings.impact: Row 4 / D5 partially unmet on the web path and web/CLI attribution diverge for the same user.
findings.recommendation: Use the platform default model when none is given so the context-time check is category-aware.

findings.title: Matrix rows 9, 10, 11, 13 not tested
findings.problem: The table-driven and end-to-end tests skip project/marketplace workflows, the nested saved assistant and datasource indexing; the row 11 gap slipped through because of that.
findings.impact: Regressions in workflow and indexing attribution go unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add end-to-end tests for rows 9, 10, 11 and 13.
